subject: Roles, timeline, and decision risks for inference deployment
messages:
From: Hannah Lane <h.lane@medsys.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-28T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up and procurement intro — inference decision criteria

Hi Aditya / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — the team found the latency/throughput conversation helpful. A couple of things we need to capture on our side so we can surface to procurement and finance:

- Decision-makers: CFO (Liam Grant) will sign economic approvals; I own the security/procurement coordination.
- Deployment preference: our infra/security folks prefer private VPC for PHI, but we could run a short pilot on hosted if the data can be tokenized/anonymized.
- Performance targets: primary customer-facing flows should be p95 inference <= 150ms end-to-end. For batch/background jobs we can accept higher latency.
- Cost sensitivity: finance wants an order-of-magnitude estimate for 1M tokens for both hosted and private setups.

Can you send a short, one-page summary that maps stakeholders + a proposed mutual action plan (key dates) and the SOC2/KMS details? Procurement will need an initial packet (I'll attach later).

Hannah Lane
Senior PM, Platform Integrations
MedSys Health
h.lane@medsys.com
(415) 555-0199

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Lane <h.lane@medsys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-28T17:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up and procurement intro — inference decision criteria

Hannah — thanks for the clear summary and the ask. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so procurement/finance/security have a single doc to react to:

1) Stakeholder map (short)
- Economic buyer: Liam Grant (CFO) — cost/commitment questions.
- Procurement: procurement@medsys.com (you indicated they'll own contract/redlines).
- Security/legal: internal security + compliance (you flagged PHI concerns).
- Integration: engineering lead (we should get name + Okta SSO point).

2) Decision criteria (as requested)
- Latency: target p95 <= 150ms for interactive flows; fallback p95 <= 250ms acceptable for degraded mode.
- Availability: 99.9% SLA for primary endpoints (we can propose 99.95% for Dedicated).
- Data handling: support for private VPC + KMS-managed keys; default retention 7 days for logs and 30 days for KV cache unless customer specifies.
- Cost: rough ballpark (very high level): Hosted API — ~$350 per 1M tokens (mixed prompt+generation) for the model class we demoed; Dedicated (reserved GPUs) — depends on commit but estimated unit cost could be ~60–70% of hosted per-token at scale (after commit). We'll provide tighter numbers once we know qps and sequence lengths.

3) Risk / open questions to surface to Liam and procurement
- If on-prem or strict air-gapped requirement: that extends legal review and delivery by ~8–12 weeks.
- If PHI is required on production data: we recommend Private deployment with customer-managed KMS; additional SOC2 attestations may be requested.
- SLA exceptions: higher SLA (99.95%) requires Dedicated capacity and a signed commitment.

4) Proposed mutual action plan (dates are suggestions)
- 2026-09-02: Procurement kickoff & SOC2/KMS exchange (30–60 min).
- 2026-09-09: Legal redline window opens (we share draft SLA & initial SOW).
- 2026-09-16: Decision checkpoint with Liam (economics + recommended deployment).
- 2026-09-30: Target go/no-go for pilot (hosted sandbox or Dedicated proofs-of-concept).

Attachments I will send in a follow-up: a concise SLA draft, SOC2 summary, and an initial mutual action plan doc. For now I attached a one-page summary and the SLA draft for your legal/procurement team to start reviewing.

Attachment: redwood-sla-draft.pdf (pdf)

Next steps: if you can confirm procurement contact and the name of the integration lead (Okta point), we’ll lock the September dates in my calendar.

— Aditya Rao
Business Development Lead | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
(650) 555-0123

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Lane <h.lane@medsys.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up and procurement intro — inference decision criteria

Thanks — adding a few contract/legal and technical clarifications from our side so procurement can pre-empt common redlines: 

- Data residency & PHI: if production requires PHI in model inputs, we need a Private deployment with customer-managed KMS and written assurance about endpoint network boundaries. That path typically adds 6–12 weeks for deployment and an implementation SOW.
- SOC2 / audit artifacts: we can provide SOC2 Type II report, pen test summary, and runbooks. Please tell us who should receive these (legal@medsys? procurement@medsys?).
- Retention & logs: default metrics logs are 7 days, request/response debug logs up to 30 days; we can extend retention to meet audit requirements in SOW (may affect cost).
- Okta SSO / SCIM provisioning: we support SAML and OIDC; if you need SCIM user provisioning we’ll scope that in the SOW (2–3 weeks to integrate).

On the economic side — to give Liam a clearer picture we can propose two commitment tiers: (A) 12-month reserved Dedicated with predictable unit costs; (B) Hosted + burst capacity for a 90-day pilot while evaluation occurs. We’ll put numbers in the SLA doc but need estimated monthly active tokens / peak qps.

Sample redline risks to flag to legal: indemnity caps, data breach notification timelines (24–72 hours), and escalation for SLA credits. If you want, we can draft a minimal mutual NDA addendum for procurement to speed SOC2 sharing.

Quote of previous for context:
> On 2026-08-28T17:02:00-07:00 Aditya Rao wrote:
> > Latency: target p95 <= 150ms for interactive flows; fallback p95 <= 250ms acceptable for degraded mode.

Happy to join the procurement kickoff — propose Wed 2026-09-02 10:00–10:45 PT.

— Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Hannah Lane <h.lane@medsys.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam Grant <liam.grant@medsys.com>, procurement@medsys.com
Date: 2026-08-30T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up and procurement intro — inference decision criteria

Aditya / Karthik — thanks, that is very helpful. Procurement packet attached and procurement@medsys.com will take the lead on contract flow. A few concrete answers: 

- Procurement contact: procurement@medsys.com (cc’d).
- Integration lead / Okta point: Nina Patel (n.patel@medsys.com) — she’ll join the kickoff.
- SOC2 & artifacts: send to procurement@medsys.com; they prefer a secure link.
- Latency: we can accept the fallback 250ms for non-critical flows, but primary customer flows must aim for p95 <= 150ms. If Redwood can commit to p95 <= 150ms on a Dedicated offering, finance is open to a 12-month commit at the rates you’ll propose.
- Timeline: procurement is aiming to complete vendor selection by 2026-09-20. The proposed kickoff on 2026-09-02 at 10:00 PT works for us.

I uploaded the procurement packet here: https://medsys.sharepoint.com/sites/procurement/packets/MS-2026-081 (procurement will also send a DocuSign link to start the SOW once redlines are resolved).

Attachments: medsys-procurement-packet.pdf

Next steps (agreed):
- Redwood to send SOC2 summary + redwood-sla-draft.pdf to procurement@medsys.com today.
- Schedule 2026-09-02 10:00 PT procurement kickoff (calendar invite to follow).
- Nina Patel (integration) to provide expected qps and sample payload sizes by 2026-09-01 so Redwood can produce a cost estimate.

Hannah Lane
Senior PM, Platform Integrations
MedSys Health
